Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told a gathering of Pacific leaders that the region’s approach to climate‑related challenges is “unified, not uniform.”

Greens can hope to pick up the mess Labor and Albanese have made

Labor’s shift to the right has opened political space on its left. If the Greens seriously want to become an alternative party of government, they must take votes from Labor, professionalise and build a much broader political movement.

Actual Article Body:
October 6, 2026

Labor’s shift to the right has opened political space on its left. If the Greens seriously want to become an alternative party of government, they must take votes from Labor, professionalise and build a much broader political movement.

The new aspiration of the Greens to be seen as an alternative party of government, rather than as a left-wing prod on the Labor Party flank, is a worthy one, capable over time of being realised. It’s not inevitable. It requires reorientation of the Greens, at both parliamentary and organisational level, and more unity of purpose and policy development. But its future cannot be defined by a sneering Labor Party. It would involve a new working relationship or set of bargains around the achievement of Labor’s agenda. And as well, a Greens agenda.
